A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, On the Challenges and Opportunities in Generative AI. Their complete text and tables support comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix; references occupy the remaining pages.

before.justification: v2 presents a literature-based discussion and research agenda. Empirical findings are attributed to cited studies; no original experiments or data analyses are reported.

after.justification: v4 remains a literature-based survey. Its new tables list challenges, resources, and prospective research questions, without reporting original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces a concrete algorithm or model developed by this work. v4 discusses additional published approaches, including heavy-tailed diffusion priors and machine unlearning, without introducing an original procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. Benchmarks newly listed in Tables 1–3, including WILDS and LongBench, are suggested research resources rather than newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Additional methods discussed in v4 participate in the literature review, not an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol is introduced or revised. Discussions of metrics, training costs, and prospective benchmark use do not constitute evaluations performed by this work.

E4.justification: Neither version reports its own ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. v4 adds discussion and research questions about these topics, without conducting the proposed analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for original results. Model uncertainty and calibration remain subjects of the survey rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Section 3 adds literature-derived numerical findings: PaLM training produces 271 tons of CO2e, with GPT-3 producing roughly twice that under comparable accounting assumptions. v2 discusses energy costs qualitatively. These are newly reported cited results, not original experiments or same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or derivations. v4's explanation of structural causal models and revised description of an ideal generative model are conceptual exposition, without new formal mathematical results.

C1.justification: The central roadmap and argument that scaling alone is insufficient remain. The introduction replaces the ideal of solving every conceivable AI task with explicit calibration, causal consistency, controllability, safety, and efficiency requirements. The conclusion adds stronger recommendations for regulatory frameworks and interdisciplinary collaboration.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands qualifications and recommendations: Section 2.3 distinguishes principled assumptions from convenience-driven choices, Section 2.4 specifies embodied-agent requirements, and Sections 4.1–4.2 expand watermarking tradeoffs, security threats, and memorization mitigation. Section 4.2 removes v2's high-resolution differential-privacy scalability caveat and adds concerns about comparing different privacy formulations.

D1.justification: Tables 1–3 add explicit links to third-party datasets and benchmark resources, including WILDS, LongBench, and HumanEval. This expands documented access information, although neither version supplies implementation or reproducibility instructions for original experiments.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands the literature across robustness, diffusion priors, efficient architectures, model selection, security, and unlearning. Examples include FlashAttention-2, zero-cost proxies, and recent security surveys. The introduction also explicitly positions the paper as an entry point across domains that complements specialized surveys.

P1.justification: Most prose and the three thematic divisions remain. v4 swaps the causal-modeling and implicit-assumptions subsections, revises the introduction and conclusion, clarifies several passages, retitles Sections 2.4 and 4.2, and updates author and publication information.

P2.justification: v2 has no tables; v4 adds three substantial five-column tables covering all three thematic divisions. They align challenges with failure modes, mitigation options, reference materials, and research questions, creating a new visual structure for navigating the survey. Publication headers and page layout also change.

improvement.justification: Tables 1–3 make v2's largely narrative roadmap easier to use by connecting specific research questions with failure modes, mitigation approaches, and resources. Clearer qualifications about assumptions and expanded privacy and security discussions improve the survey's guidance. Some citation weaknesses remain, including duplicate Golechha and Dao 2024a/b entries and unclear support for the new healthcare example in Section 4.5. The net improvement is useful but limited.
